title: Jewellery Catalogue Maker for WhatsApp | OneCatalog
description: A jewellery catalogue maker for jewellers and wholesalers. Show weight, purity and designs in one link, and let buyers ask price on WhatsApp.
h1: Jewellery catalogue maker that works when the gold rate changes every day
answer: OneCatalog is a jewellery catalogue maker for jewellery shops and wholesalers. We build a catalogue where every design has its own page with photos, weight and purity. Because gold prices move daily, most jewellers show Price on request and quote the day's price in the WhatsApp chat.
waText: Hi OneCatalog, I want a catalogue for my jewellery business.

mockup.label: Sample jewellery catalogue showing weight and purity, shown on a phone

sections.h2: Why jewellers struggle to share designs on WhatsApp

blocks.p: Picture a jewellery wholesaler in Chennai who supplies 60 retail shops. Every new design goes out as a photo with the weight typed underneath. Retailers ask for the photo again a week later. Some forward old photos with old weights to their own customers.

pain: Weight and purity get lost when a photo is forwarded without the caption.
A price typed on a photo is wrong the next day when the gold rate moves.
Customers ask to see all the designs in a range, and you send them in batches of ten.

sections.h2: How a jewellery catalogue maker helps

blocks.p: In a catalogue, the weight and purity sit on the product page with the photos. They never get separated. A retailer or customer opens one link and sees every design in the range.

Price stays in your hands. Most jewellers use Price on request for gold, so the catalogue never shows an out-of-date price. The customer taps Enquire on WhatsApp, the message names the exact design, and you quote today's rate in the chat. Fixed-price items like silver or imitation jewellery can show a price.

blocks.p: Give every design a code. The code appears in the customer's WhatsApp message, so you know which piece they mean even if two designs look alike.
No. A OneCatalog catalogue is a public web page. Anyone with the link can see it, and Google can list it. That is what helps new customers find you.

ul: Use a plain dark or white cloth as the background. Busy backgrounds hide the detail.
Shoot in soft daylight. Direct sun makes gold look white and flat.
Take one full photo and one close-up of the work, such as stone setting or filigree.
Keep a small ruler or coin out of the photo and write the size in the details instead.
Hold the phone steady or rest it on a box. Blurred jewellery photos cannot be fixed later.

blocks.p: Jewellers with a focused range start with up to 50 designs for ₹3,999 in the first year. Wholesalers with more designs choose 150 or 300 products. Compare them on the [pricing page](/pricing), and see how sharing works on our [WhatsApp catalogue page](/whatsapp-catalogue). If you supply other shops, the [wholesale catalogue page](/catalogue-maker/wholesale) covers MOQ and bulk orders.

items.q: Can I show the weight and purity of each design?
items.a: Yes. Weight in grams, purity and stone details go on each product page, right next to the photos.

items.q: How do I handle prices that change with the gold rate?
items.a: Show Price on request for gold items. Customers tap Enquire on WhatsApp and you quote the day's price in the chat. Items with a fixed price, like silver, can show it.

items.q: Can I hide designs from the public?
items.a: No. The catalogue is a public link. Keep exclusive designs out of it and share them in private chats.

items.q: Can I list making charges or wastage?
items.a: Yes. Write them in the product details, for example making charges as a percentage. They appear on the product page with the weight and purity, so customers see them before they ask.

items.q: Can retailers share my catalogue with their customers?
items.a: Yes. They can forward your link. Every enquiry from it comes to your WhatsApp number, whoever forwarded it.
